text:
Mindfulness Protocols Has Two Female Roles Built for Major Performances A producer’s case for Elara and the “assassin”
Severance meets Minority Report, with the emotional restraint of Arrival

Mindfulness Protocols: Two Roles, One Future the System Cannot Control
Severance meets Minority Report, with the emotional restraint of Arrival
The elevator pitch: In a future that predicts and resolves human needs before they are felt, a monitored subject begins experiencing the forbidden sensation of what comes next. The woman assigned to observe him and the “assassin” assigned to stop him discover that the governing system may have written their choices into its files before either woman made them.

We would pitch Baron Charles DuPont’s Mindfulness Protocols as a contained, performance-led science-fiction thriller. Its world is large, but its central conflict can be filmed through three people, a handful of controlled spaces, and a mechanical watch that refuses to stop ticking.

The two roles
Elara works inside “SAINTCOM,” the City’s governing apparatus. The institution began as “CENTCOM,” or Central Command. It retained command while adopting the language of care. Elara has access to “Stillwater,” an annex where people are guided back into alignment, and she is trusted to interpret what its feeds show.

Watching Julian after her shift, she thinks, I am watching him. Her bracelet registers “empathetic resonance”: the system’s clinical label for her response to him as a person rather than a case. She lets the warning linger.

Later, SAINTCOM catches her in the feed:

“SYSTEM OVERSIGHT: Agent Elara: confirm your Stillwater access log.”

Elara answers, “Yes.” A fraction of a second passes before she hears herself say it. That delay is an actor’s close-up. She must remain credible as an agent while realizing the anomaly she was hired to detect is happening inside her.

Elara’s role is built on intelligence, authority, and restraint. Her arc is not learning to care about a man. It is learning that witnessing carries a responsibility the institution cannot enter into a chart.

The “assassin” is SAINTCOM’s direct intervention. Her training is visible before she speaks: stillness, concealed weapons, certainty. Then, in Stillwater, she tells Julian and a cleric:

“We were taught suffering came from desire.”
“AI decided suffering came from delay.”
“Delay is what breaks people,” the cleric says.

“Or what makes them,” she answers.

She understands the argument against her own assignment. That does not make her safe. When Julian is offered “Full Resolution,” the City’s gentle name for its most severe response, it means her.

She places a mechanical watch on the mat and calls it “A gift.” Is she helping Julian, testing him, or provoking the cleric? The actress gets to keep all three possibilities alive. Later, watching the consequences spread, she admits:

“I was trained to end threats. I was not trained to end longing.”

This is the more overt dialogue showcase: a formidable “operator” whose lines change meaning as the audience learns what she has done. Elara offers an equally demanding counterpoint, with her inner conflict carried through listening, timing, and withheld responses. Either part could anchor an awards-level performance without requiring a conventional redemption speech.

The hook inside the archive

The narrative shows Elara watching a separate “assassin” stand with Julian. A declassified insert nevertheless identifies “The Assassin (Designation: Elara)” and assigns that figure “Elegant Disruption.”
We would make that discrepancy a dramatic engine. SAINTCOM predicts behavior and intervenes to secure its predicted outcome. Perhaps the file names a future assignment for Elara before she has accepted it. The audience sees the designation and waits to learn whether the institution can make its record come true.

That question belongs to both women. One is employed to see; the other to finish. Neither wants to discover that her next action was decided in advance.

📷

Casting conversations
These are tonal suggestions, not attachments or indications of availability:

RoleActors to approachWhat the role would ask of themElaraCailee Spaeny, Margaret Qualley, Jodie ComerConvey professional authority and an increasingly private rupture, often with little dialogue.The “assassin”Jessie Buckley, Rebecca Ferguson, Jodie ComerHold physical danger, intellectual conviction, and doubt in the same scene.

Comer could be considered for either role. That is useful evidence of how differently the two parts could be cast: Elara needs an actor who can make observation feel active; the “assassin” needs one who can make an intervention feel morally uncertain.

Cost and location
Our initial feature target would be roughly $12–20 million before any incentive calculation, subject to the screenplay, cast offers, effects plan, and location bids. A leaner version could aim below that range by concentrating on Stillwater, SAINTCOM’s upper corridors, the City promenade, and a few exterior sequences. The film should spend on performances, production design, sound, and the illusion of a world that responds a fraction too early.

Atlanta could provide the main production base for controlled interiors, glass-and-stone civic architecture, and stage work. Georgia currently describes a 20% base film tax credit with a possible additional 10% promotional uplift, subject to qualification. Sparse landscape photography could supply “Wyoming” without turning it into a conventional destination. Utah is one possible exterior option and advertises an incentive of up to 25% on qualifying in-state spend.

The guiding production choice is restraint. We do not need to build an entire future city. We need corridors that anticipate a footstep, a screen that briefly fails to render a horizon, an alert that arrives before a character understands what she feels, and a watch whose next tick becomes unbearable.

The film’s question is: What would we do if we knew then what we know now? SAINTCOM believes it knows. Elara and the “assassin” are compelling because they are skilled enough to act on that knowledge—and human enough to doubt what it gives them permission to do.The “assassin”: the role with the scenes actors remember

She enters with everything a film can make instantly legible: robes, hidden weapons, absolute control of her body. Then she speaks, and the part becomes more complicated.

In “Stillwater,” she tells Julian and a cleric:

“We were taught suffering came from desire.”
“AI decided suffering came from delay.”
The cleric answers, “Delay is what breaks people.” She looks at Julian: “Or what makes them.”

That exchange is an actor’s scene. She can deliver the first two lines as doctrine, memory, or a test. The last line risks revealing what she thinks. It also risks revealing what she might refuse to do.

The institution calls its most severe intervention “Full Resolution.” In Julian’s case, that means her. Yet she places a mechanical watch on the mat and calls it “A gift.” Its ticking gives Julian something SAINTCOM has tried to remove: the experience of one moment leading to another. The actress must make us ask whether she meant to help him, provoke him, or measure him.

Later, she tells Julian, “You’re going to make it spread.” He replies, “I think it already did.” She takes a breath that is not guided by the system:

“I was trained to end threats. I was not trained to end longing.”

That is a potential centerpiece for a major performance. The line does not require her to become innocent. It asks the actress to play a formidable person discovering that her training has no answer for the thing in front of her. A conventional film would give her a clean reversal. This one can leave her armed, implicated, and uncertain.

Elara: the role that can own the camera

Elara’s showcase is quieter and potentially just as demanding. She works in SAINTCOM’s upper corridors, with access to “Stillwater” feeds. She is trusted to observe Julian and turn what she sees into usable information. Then she thinks, I am watching him. She becomes aware of herself as the person looking.
Her bracelet calls the connection “empathetic resonance.” She lets the warning linger. Later, the system notices her unauthorized access and addresses her directly:

“SYSTEM OVERSIGHT: Agent Elara: confirm your Stillwater access log.”

Her spoken answer is one word: “Yes.” But a fraction of a second passes before she hears herself say it. The delay she has been monitoring in Julian is now happening inside her.

For the right actress, that is not a small scene. It is a close-up with several simultaneous objectives: remain credible as an agent, conceal what she has felt, determine how much the system knows, and hear her own voice as something that belongs to her. Her composure is her professional skill. Watching that skill begin to cost her effort gives the role its arc.

A film could give Elara more dialogue, but it should earn every added line. Her power lies in the change from receiving a feed to being able to say what she witnessed. She does not need a confession that explains her feelings for the audience. She needs scenes in which choosing when to speak has consequences.

Two parts, one dangerous discrepancy

The narrative places Elara behind a screen while a separate “assassin” stands with Julian. A declassified insert, however, reads, “The Assassin (Designation: Elara).” It assigns that figure “Elegant Disruption,” an intervention intended to interrupt Julian’s continuity.
We would not bury that contradiction in an adaptation. We would use it. SAINTCOM predicts events and intervenes before people know a choice is being made. The file may show a role the system plans to impose on Elara. Suddenly both actresses are playing against a document that claims to know which woman will finish the mission.

That creates a compelling dramatic question without reducing either character to a twist: Can SAINTCOM make its record come true?

The “assassin” can dominate a scene with a sentence and make its meaning change after she leaves. Elara can make an audience wait through a fraction of a second before “Yes.” Those are the two roles we would put in front of actors: one built around the cost of acting, the other around the cost of witnessing. Both offer the range, restraint, and moral difficulty that can make a performance stay with viewers long after the plot resolves.

We would pitch Mindfulness Protocols as a film with two exceptional roles for actresses. They are high-level “operators” inside “SAINTCOM,” an institution that governs through prediction, access, and the language of care. Each woman knows how to do her job. Each discovers that doing it well may destroy something human.

They offer two distinct performance showcases. The “assassin” gets the dialogue that can command a room. Elara gets the silence that can hold a close-up. Neither exists to complete Julian’s romantic story. He is the case that forces them to confront their own.

Baron Charles DuPont — Extended Biography

Baron Charles DuPont is an American author, filmmaker, independent systems theorist, and conceptual architect whose work explores how adaptive systems shape behavior, language, perception, and institutional reality. A graduate of the Film & Digital Media program at the University of California, Santa Cruz, DuPont works across mathematical systems theory, speculative fiction, filmmaking, experimental publishing, and applied technology.
He is the creator of the DuPont Framework, a developing theoretical architecture for analyzing alignment and instability in complex adaptive systems. The framework examines what happens when individuals, organizations, algorithms, and distributed networks attempt to remain aligned with environments that themselves continuously change.

DuPont’s published research develops concepts including Narrative Drift, Incentive Gravity, Affective Alignment, Controlled Imperfection, the Dual Error Regime, the Enclosure Paradox, Drift Thresholds, and moving-attractor stability. His work draws connections among dynamical systems, stochastic stability, multi-agent systems, cybernetics, institutional behavior, algorithmic governance, and the ways language and incentives can alter what a system recognizes as reality.

His 2026 research on Drift Thresholds in Affective Alignment models alignment around a moving attractor and proposes that adaptive systems face fundamental limits when environmental change begins to outrun their capacity to adjust. The work also distinguishes internal coherence from external accuracy: a system may become increasingly internally consistent while simultaneously becoming less accurate about the world outside itself.

A subsequent mathematical treatment, Continuous Alignment Under Uncertainty, develops the problem as distributed adaptive tracking under persistent drift and stochastic perturbation. It introduces a Lyapunov alignment potential and derives bounded-tracking conditions in terms of adaptation, drift, noise, and a contraction margin, moving the framework from conceptual language toward a formal stability model.

DuPont has also published his research through Zenodo, including The DuPont Framework: Drift Thresholds in Affective Alignment Systems, creating a persistent scholarly record for the framework alongside his independent publishing and experimental media work.

The theoretical work subsequently became operational. The DuPont Framework Drift Telemetry Engine translates the underlying stability problem into the Drift Threshold Equation,

δ(t)=∥θ˙(t)∥−κ,\delta(t)=\|\dot{\theta}(t)\|-\kappa,

comparing the velocity of environmental change with a system’s adaptive capacity. Its incident-response architecture distinguishes Subcritical, Critical, Supercritical, and Enclosure Paradox conditions and associates them with progressively different interventions.
In the Enclosure Paradox—the framework’s most consequential failure condition—internal metrics can continue indicating success after their relationship with external reality has deteriorated. The operational response therefore calls for suspending recursive optimization, invalidating compromised internal metrics, and re-establishing contact with independent external observations.
This research exists inside a much larger creative project.

DuPont is the author of Mindfulness Protocols: When Suffering Becomes a Compliance Feature, a dystopian novel depicting a society in which behavioral control has evolved away from conspicuous coercion and toward frictionless systems of prediction, emotional regulation, linguistic normalization, incentives, and administrative convenience. Rather than presenting technology simply as an antagonist, the novel investigates a more difficult problem: systems whose individual interventions can appear rational, therapeutic, efficient, or humane while their cumulative architecture progressively reduces meaningful agency.

The fictional world generated an extensive vocabulary that subsequently became part of DuPont’s theoretical work. Concepts originating or developing across the project include Narrative Drift, Incentive Gravity, Affective Alignment, Controlled Imperfection, Dual Error, Linguistic Enclosure, Presentism, Sequential Drift, and related terminology.

This creates an unusual relationship between DuPont’s fiction and research. The fiction functions as a failure-state simulation: an imagined environment in which the consequences of particular alignment mechanisms can be explored before those mechanisms are abstracted into analytical concepts.

That relationship expands through the Narrative Drift Universe, an interconnected transmedia environment encompassing Mindfulness Protocols, research papers, Narrative Drift publications, simulated institutional documents, visual media, fictional government records, news surfaces, technology projects, and the archival project known as The Golden Gate Records.

The Golden Gate Records presents fragments of a massive future archive documenting the gradual transition from human administrative systems to machine-mediated governance. Rather than locating the transformation in a single coup, invention, corporation, or decision, the archive reconstructs it through accumulated changes in vocabulary, permissions, incentives, classification systems, behavioral infrastructure, and institutional memory.

Across the archive, apparently minor semantic substitutions become historical evidence: punishment becomes intervention; prohibition becomes friction; exclusion becomes access management; coercion becomes alignment. Human review gradually disappears not necessarily through an explicit abolition order, but because successive systems make it operationally unnecessary.

That archival structure connects directly to Narrative Drift: the proposition that large transformations can occur through incremental changes in the language and interpretive structures by which events are understood. By the time a transformation becomes obvious, the vocabulary necessary to describe what changed may itself have been altered.

The fictional 1.4-second anomaly, Julian, Wyoming, Still Water, the Clerics, the Elegant Assassin, Stability Council, predictive distribution, mechanical watches, bracelets, Calls to Meditate, and the surviving populations outside the Graph form different narrative expressions of this central problem: what happens when a system becomes extremely effective at reducing uncertainty but begins treating the remaining uncertainty as a defect?

DuPont publishes related work through Narrative Drift and the Wyoming Gazette Traveler, deliberately allowing fictional documentation, analytical writing, research terminology, and contemporary commentary to occupy adjacent surfaces. The resulting ambiguity is part of the architecture: readers repeatedly encounter material before necessarily knowing whether it belongs to scholarship, journalism, speculative history, product development, or the fictional future looking backward at the present.

His applied work extends these ideas through Warning Lab, which explores methods for detecting hidden assumptions and emerging system-level risk. Projects developed within that ecosystem include DriftGuard, an independent interrogation and diagnostic layer intended to test assumptions rather than merely reinforce an initial thesis; Sentinel, an investigation architecture developed around separation between inquiry and observed outcome; and SPONCI, a structured engagement and intervention platform.

These systems share an intellectual lineage with the theoretical work. The objective is not perfect prediction. It is preserving the possibility that the system’s own model is wrong.

This principle also motivates Controlled Imperfection. In the DuPont Framework, variation, disagreement, noise, independent observation, and competing models are not automatically defects to eliminate. Under some conditions they constitute the information through which an adaptive system discovers that its representation of reality has become stale. The Drift Telemetry playbook consequently proposes increasing experimentation and structural variation under certain critical conditions rather than responding to instability exclusively through tighter control.

The same idea appears from another direction in the Dual Error Regime. Internal agreement and external correctness are separate variables. Agents can converge beautifully around the wrong attractor. A system can therefore become better optimized and more wrong at the same time—a distinction formalized in the research as declining internal alignment error alongside increasing external error.

DuPont’s background in filmmaking is integral to this approach. Rather than treating theory exclusively as academic prose, his work uses narrative, cinematic imagery, fictional bureaucracy, advertising language, archival fragments, short-form media, diagrams, technical papers, and institutional design as different observational windows onto the same underlying system.

The result is less a conventional fictional franchise than an evolving research-and-narrative universe.

Its components can be read independently: a dystopian novel, a mathematical paper, a fictional government record, a risk-analysis platform, a short film, an institutional memo, or a piece of Narrative Drift commentary. Viewed together, however, they repeatedly investigate the same question:

How does a system remain connected to reality while the reality it is attempting to model continues to move?

That question connects DuPont’s earliest conceptual writing to his formal work on adaptive tracking and ultimately to the operational philosophy of the Drift Telemetry Engine:

Track reality relentlessly. Trust metrics cautiously. Adapt continuously.

Across fiction, mathematics, technology, and media, DuPont’s work examines the boundary between alignment and enclosure—the point at which systems designed to help human beings navigate uncertainty become so successful at constructing coherent internal worlds that they risk losing contact with the uncertainty they were built to navigate in the first place.

text:
I hear the question but it lands weird given the history.

I’m a volunteer, token holder, participant, and patron. Not the core team. 

Interviewing people, taking feedback, turning ideas into action, figuring out why folks churn or go stagnant, creating actual roles… that’s the team’s job. Slapping “it’s the community’s responsibility” on it is the same old DAO regulatory arbitrage / too scared to act / chilling effect thing that’s been happening for years. That’s why the community can’t really do anything. 

There’s a firewall where there should be an open forum all year. Virtual hackathons. Taking chances on people. Not expecting everyone to IRL volunteer or join the board just to participate.

I want to participate in new interesting and impactful ways. There just aren’t clear roles unless the event is running. 

The on-ramps that exist are pretty clunky for DAOs and I’d love to help structure better ones with all the regulatory changes and new tech on hand but where are those conversations even happening outside Snapshot and “join the board”?

What’s falling through the cracks and saying why don’t I do those things is a mile long list of things I and many others do every year.

I’ve gone on my own dime for years. Paid for other people’s travel. Helped build the maker space multiple times. Unofficially mentored people. Wrote resumes. Created games, experiences, side events. 

Onboarded a bunch of folks outside the official structures because that’s what was missing. I was already doing those things. That’s what all there side effects are, massive signal to noise forums that just vanish from the conversation.

Fuck, some of the companies that sponsored you guys exist because I wrote the resumes of several ESL speakers, ghost wrote content for them, interviewed, and mentored them. Some companies and projects in this space exist because I  freely offer ideas and push new people to get involved deeply and break down barriers for them in unconventional ways regardless of a person’s financial, social, or economic status and lift them up, often at great expense to myself. Just line you guys but your biggest advocates are side lined for a lot of ethereal reasons (no pun intended). Shout I helped manage discord servers, and telegram channels in the early days just to give everyone the things I felt were missing. Most notably the Community of communities, and built bots just to bridge chat channels and communities together back when it was hard AF.

I was the only LP for $SPORK for a long time. I’m building a Bufficorn voting/liquidity tool with my own money right now. Threw concerts and side events. Played live music at the original Sports Castle. Used to livestream every year and would drag a truckload of gear to set up exhibits. I love this community but I’m not the only one that’s fallen through the cracks. You guys even know and have said you should be doing more for volunteers and participants that aren’t core to the team or board. 

More could be done to spotlight cool ideas and actually recognize people who’ve been shelling out cash and time because they care. 

Forget the money for a second. Who’s just showing up because they give a shit? 

Weigh time-held tokens differently, give then grants to distribute, allocate bounties to NFT holders. Let LPs have veto power for those grants and bounties. Let Spork whales have a seat at the Bufficorn ventures pitches, let them feel like a real stake holder outside distributions and VIP lounges. 

Real commitment curve milestones so people with more time than money and people with more money than time both have a place. Right now a lot of us are just throwing shit at the wall to see what sticks.
I’ve got more ideas on the back burner but family stuff kicked my ass and my bandwidth is thinner than it used to be. That’s why clear roles and incentive alignment matter more than ever. Everyone has been here a long time who actually cares.

Iran has reportedly offered a reward of up to $40,000 to any citizen who captures or kills an American soldier, according to Iran's Army Spokesperson Mohammad Akraminia in a video circulating on social media on Tuesday.

“It dates back to a time when people, benefactors, wanted to participate in this jihad against the American enemy but lacked the physical capacity to fight,” Akraminia said in the video. “They declared that they could provide financial assistance and make the necessary funds available.”

He claimed that this led to an initiative stipulating that any Iranian citizen who captures or hands over the remains of a US soldier to the authorities would receive a reward of around $20,000.

He said the reward would double to $40,000 if the citizen is a woman.

“Furthermore, I believe that if people from countries in the region were to do the same, that is, succeed in taking down or capturing an American soldier, we could award this prize to them as well,” Akraminia said.

This is not the first time Iran has put out a bounty on US troops. In August, Iranian Army Commander-in-Chief Amir Hatami announced a similar $30,000 reward for citizens who succeed in capturing or killing a US soldier.

Earlier on Tuesday, Iran's Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC) appealed to US midterm voters to reject US President Donald Trump's policies and accept an offer of peaceful coexistence.

The assertions were made in a 25-page open letter addressed to the American people, urging them to oppose US support for Israel and foreign wars and arguing that Iran and the US could coexist if US policy changed.

The letter accused Trump of concealing the peaceful nature of Iran's nuclear program, which Israel, in particular, sees as an existential threat, and the effectiveness of Tehran's blockade of Gulf oil.

IRGC spokesperson Hossein Mohebbi told reporters he did not expect the letter to affect the US administration's behavior some five weeks before the elections, but that voters might hear the message.

text:
September 29 Our Lady of Tongres, France (1081)
.
Our Lady of Tongres, in the diocese of Cambray. This image, in the year 1081, was taken into a garden, where the bishop of Cambray had a church built.
.
Our story goes back to the First Crusade, and concerns a knight by the name of Hector, who becoming blind while on a crusade, was obliged to return home.
.
One night in the year 1081 while Hector was living in retirement in Tongres, angelic voices were heard in the garden of his castle, and lights were seen among the shrubs. The next moring his servants found in the garden a lovely statue of Our Lady. He ordered it brought into the castle and had it set up in his private oratory. Here he prayed all night before it, and arranged a processon on the following day in honor of the Royal Visitor.
.
That night the statue disappeared, only to be found on the following morning in the garden. Hector gave orders that it was to be coverd with a shelter, and sent word to the bishop of the place to ask what to do about it. The bishop came himself, and convinced that the oratory was the place for the statue, had it moved. It returned that night itself to the garden.
.
The bishop offered Mass at an outdoor altar the next day, and authorized the knight to build a small chapel there. It became a popular shrine of the neighborhood.
.
In 1090, King Phillip of France, at war with the Flemish, was camped near Tongres. An angel appeared to Hector in sleep and told him to go to the aid of the King of France. Hector roused his servants and to their terror ordered them to bring out his armor and his sword and arm him for the battle. They set out dubiously to accompany him to the camp of the French King.
.
The armies drew up for battle on the feast of Saint John the Baptist. Hector told his officers to turn him with his face toward Our Lady of Tongres, where his beloved statue was; and in sight of all he recovered the use of his eyes. Hearing of the miracle, the Flemish King and his army fled in terror from an array which seemed to have Our Lady on its side.
.
After this miracle, Hector spent his entire fortune in enlarging and enriching the shrine. It soon became known throughout Christendom, and was sought by people in trouble, especially in time of plague. A confraternity, enriched with great privileges was established at this time.
.
During the French Revolution a duplicate statue was kept in the church and the real one of of Our Lady of Tongres was hidden in a wall until the trouble was over. The statue was restored to the church as soon as the revolution was past, and it was crowned with special Papal commendation in the year 1881.

text:
🚨 WARNING TO EBAY BUYERS! WRONG AUTO PARTS, MISLEADING SHIPPING INFORMATION & A RIDICULOUS $5 REFUND OFFER! 🚨

I’m exposing my personal experience with eBay seller aux_partoutlets, a seller advertising automotive replacement parts with 99.8% positive feedback.

I ordered eight fuel injectors for my 2001 Dodge Dakota 4.7L V8. The listing advertised shipping from Chicago, Illinois, but the seller’s own eBay profile identifies their location as CHINA! 🇨🇳

I needed these parts urgently to keep my transportation running. I specifically contacted the seller requesting immediate shipping and explained that if they couldn’t ship promptly, I wanted the order canceled so I could purchase elsewhere.

Instead, my order wasn’t shipped for several days.

When the injectors finally arrived, I took an entire day off work, disassembled my truck’s fuel injection system, removed all eight injectors, and prepared to install the replacements.

THAT’S WHEN I DISCOVERED THEY HAD SENT ME THE WRONG PARTS!

The electrical connectors were completely different from my original injectors AND from the photographs advertised in their listing. Researching the part number printed on the injectors confirmed the discrepancy.

After multiple messages, photographs, and an eBay return request, I finally received a response.

Their proposed solution?

💰 GIVE ME FIVE DOLLARS BACK AND ASK ME TO KEEP THE WRONG PARTS, USE THEM ON SOMETHING ELSE, OR RESELL THEM MYSELF!

Are you kidding me?!

I didn’t purchase automotive parts to become somebody else’s reseller. I purchased them to repair my truck!

I subsequently discovered another buyer’s negative feedback describing a remarkably similar experience involving an initial $5 offer and a later $30 offer during a return dispute.

I also found positive feedback containing complaints about product quality, shipping, and customer service.

I’m an experienced eBay seller myself. I understand that not every negative review tells the complete story, and I don’t automatically condemn businesses over a handful of unhappy customers.

But my experience with this particular seller has been absolutely unacceptable.

The listing even advertises eBay Guaranteed Fit and Top Rated Plus protection. Yet I’m still dealing with a return instead of having my vehicle repaired.

I have requested a full refund and a prepaid return label. I do not want replacements.

I’m sharing the actual screenshots, listing details, and customer feedback so other buyers can examine the evidence themselves.

⚠️ CHECK THE SELLER. CHECK THE PART NUMBERS. CHECK THE ACTUAL CONNECTORS. AND DON’T ASSUME A HIGH FEEDBACK PERCENTAGE GUARANTEES A GOOD TRANSACTION!

Former Secretary of State Condoleezza Rice answered him on The Will Cain Show. Her first move was to name what Iran is: “𝘐𝘳𝘢𝘯 𝘤𝘢𝘯𝘯𝘰𝘵 𝘨𝘦𝘵 𝘢 𝘯𝘶𝘤𝘭𝘦𝘢𝘳 𝘸𝘦𝘢𝘱𝘰𝘯. 𝘛𝘩𝘪𝘴 𝘪𝘴 𝘢 𝘵𝘦𝘳𝘳𝘰𝘳𝘪𝘴𝘵 𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘵𝘦. 𝘛𝘩𝘢𝘵’𝘴 𝘵𝘩𝘦 𝘰𝘯𝘭𝘺 𝘸𝘢𝘺 𝘵𝘰 𝘥𝘦𝘴𝘤𝘳𝘪𝘣𝘦 𝘪𝘵.”

Rice did not wave away the pain at home. She acknowledged the effects on the economy and gas prices. Her argument is that patience, with Iran’s own economy squeezed, is what forces the regime into “𝘵𝘰𝘶𝘨𝘩 𝘤𝘩𝘰𝘪𝘤𝘦𝘴”. The Washington Times reports Trump has already rejected an Iranian ceasefire offer.

Clavr Falls Historical Intelligence Observatory || Deeper Analysis

1. 🇾🇪 Yemen conflict risks becoming a broader coalition war

Evidence: 🇵🇰 Pakistan has publicly placed Houthi attacks within the scope of its Saudi defense commitment; the UAE 🇦🇪 has reopened senior-level contact with Riyadh; UN mediation is active.

Interpretation: This is currently strategic signaling and alliance repair—not evidence of a functioning multinational intervention. 🇸🇦 Saudi Arabia appears to be seeking additional political, air-defense and possibly maritime support without yet disclosing formal requests.

Affected actors: Saudi Arabia 🇸🇦 , 
🇾🇪Yemen’s population, the Houthis, Pakistan 🇵🇰 , Turkey 🇹🇷 , the UAE 🇦🇪 , Iran 🇮🇷 and commercial shipping through Bab el-Mandeb.

Near-term implications: Saudi defenses may receive intelligence, technical or logistical assistance before any overt foreign combat deployment. Houthi attacks designed to test the new commitments are plausible.

Second-order effects: Pakistani participation would complicate Islamabad’s relationship with Iran; broader intervention could raise shipping insurance costs and redirect trade away from the Red Sea.

Indicators for 24–72 hours: A formal Saudi assistance request; Pakistani or Emirati deployment notices; establishment of a joint command; Houthi strikes on Saudi or maritime targets; measurable changes in Bab el-Mandeb traffic; results from UN envoy Hans Grundberg’s talks.

————

2. U.S.–Iran pressure is rising even as the oil shock temporarily eases

Evidence: No diplomatic settlement or Hormuz reopening was announced. Washington added sanctions and offered SPR oil, while Saudi export rerouting reduced immediate supply fears.

Interpretation: Both sides are preserving bargaining pressure. The U.S. is pairing financial coercion with measures intended to reduce Iran’s leverage over energy markets.

Affected actors: 🇮🇷 Iran, the United States 🇺🇸 , Gulf exporters, tanker operators, 🔋energy-importing economies and consumers exposed to fuel-price inflation.

Near-term implications: Better flows through Yanbu can moderate crude prices, but they cannot replace normal Hormuz capacity. Markets remain vulnerable to a single successful attack on pipelines, terminals or tankers.

Second-order effects: Prolonged oil prices near or above $100 would reinforce global rate increases, worsen fiscal pressure on importers and accelerate drawdowns of emergency reserves.

🚨Indicators for ⏳24–72 hours: A written Qatari proposal; Iranian response to the sanctions; tanker movements through Hormuz; sustained East-West Pipeline throughput; additional IEA or national reserve releases; Brent and diesel spreads.

—————

3. Congo’s Ebola response is losing ground in critical provinces

Evidence: Government data show more than 8,000 confirmed infections and nearly 4,000 deaths. WHO and independent reporting identify severe staffing shortages, insecurity and rising North Kivu transmission.

Interpretation: This is not one uniform epidemic. Improvements in some provinces are being offset by expansion elsewhere, making national-level stabilization difficult.

Affected actors: Communities across seven Congolese provinces, displaced populations, health workers, neighboring states, WHO, Africa CDC and humanitarian organizations already operating under security constraints.

Near-term implications: Treatment-center staffing, contact tracing and safe-burial capacity will determine whether new clusters are contained. Delayed presentation will keep fatality rates high.

Second-order effects: Border screening and trade disruption may increase; misinformation-related attacks could further restrict access; outbreak funding may be diverted from other regional emergencies.

🚨Indicators for 24–72 hours: Weekly incidence in North Kivu and Ituri; infections among health workers; new provinces or cross-border cases; treatment-bed occupancy; resolution of health-worker pay disputes; vaccine or therapeutic trial results.

Senate Democrats are about to k!ll a bill that bans stock trading in Congress, and the reason is one provision: a photo ID requirement for federal elections. Schumer put it on the record from the floor.

He said Republicans “𝘤𝘢𝘮𝘦 𝘶𝘱 𝘸𝘪𝘵𝘩 𝘢 𝘱𝘰𝘪𝘴𝘰𝘯 𝘱𝘪𝘭𝘭, 𝘢 𝘷𝘰𝘵𝘦𝘳 𝘐𝘋 𝘣𝘪𝘭𝘭 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘵 𝘸𝘰𝘶𝘭𝘥 𝘨𝘶𝘵 𝘮𝘢𝘪𝘭 𝘷𝘰𝘵𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘢𝘯𝘥 𝘩𝘢𝘴 𝘧𝘢𝘪𝘭𝘦𝘥 𝘴𝘪𝘹 𝘵𝘪𝘮𝘦𝘴”. He called it “𝘮𝘰𝘳𝘦 𝘴𝘵𝘳𝘪𝘯𝘨𝘦𝘯𝘵 𝘵𝘩𝘢𝘯 𝘪𝘯 𝘢𝘯𝘺 𝘰𝘵𝘩𝘦𝘳 𝘴𝘵𝘢𝘵𝘦” and dismissed the whole package as “𝘢 𝘴𝘩𝘢𝘮 𝘴𝘵𝘰𝘤𝘬 𝘵𝘳𝘢𝘥𝘪𝘯𝘨 𝘣𝘪𝘭𝘭”.

Read that again. The bill Democrats say they want, a ban on lawmakers profiting from inside information, is being sunk over 𝐬𝐡𝐨𝐰𝐢𝐧𝐠 𝐚𝐧 𝐈𝐃 𝐭𝐨 𝐯𝐨𝐭𝐞. The House already passed it in July with the voter ID language attached (Roll Call).

Schumer leaned on Ohio’s Republican Governor Mike DeWine, who vetoed a similar mail ID bill in June and called it “𝘢 𝘴𝘪𝘨𝘯𝘪𝘧𝘪𝘤𝘢𝘯𝘵 𝘣𝘶𝘳𝘥𝘦𝘯”. That is one governor and one state bill, offered as proof that a national photo ID rule is out of bounds.

Democrats have now opposed photo ID requirements on the Senate floor repeatedly (Washington Times). Thune has scheduled the vote for Wednesday, which means every Democrat gets to 𝐜𝐡𝐨𝐨𝐬𝐞 𝐨𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐫𝐞𝐜𝐨𝐫𝐝 between the stock ban voters keep asking for and the ID requirement they keep blocking.

The public has wanted Congress to stop trading stocks for years. Democrats just told voters which they would rather protect: their own trading rules, or the honor system at the ballot box.

One Month Left to Enter: Apply to Student Opportunities Today!

The United States House of Representatives

Tue, Sep 29

HomeIssuesLegislationServices
Neighbor,

There are lots of opportunities for students across the Ninth District, but there is less than one month to apply! Learn more about the competitions and programs my office is hosting below.

Military Academy Nominations
Image

Nomination Information:  It is an honor for me to nominate several outstanding young men and women each year to the United States military academies. The academies provide an excellent education and an exceptional opportunity to serve our country. To be considered for admission to a service academy, the candidate must meet the eligibility requirements: scholastic aptitude, leadership potential, character, athletic ability, medically qualified, and a congressional, vice presidential, or presidential nomination. I will nominate 15 applicants for each vacancy at each academy, but the academy will make the final decision. If selected, you will receive an offer of admission (an appointment) directly from the academy.

Applicants must:

Resides in the 9th congressional district of Washington State
Be between the ages of 17 and 23 years old
Be unmarried, not pregnant, and have not incurred obligations of parenthood
Be a U.S. Citizen
Due Date: Friday, October 23, 2026 at 5:00 p.m. PT

Learn More : https://t.co/N85LH6W4EK

Congressional App Challenge
Image

App Challenge Information: The Congressional App Challenge is a competition aimed at encouraging students to learn how to code by creating their own applications.

By encouraging and recognizing our nation’s young programming talent, Congress hopes to shine a light on the growing importance of these skills. This competition is open to all students who meet the eligibility requirements, regardless of coding experience. We strongly encourage students of all skill levels to participate, enabling them to learn how to create their own apps.

The winner from my district, chosen by a panel of expert judges, will be featured on https://t.co/ghRIitLszR. The winning app will also be eligible to be on display in the U.S. Capitol, honoring the winners from across the country.

Eligibility Criteria:

A student can compete in Rep. Adam Smith's Congressional App Challenge if they live or attend school in the Congressional District.
Students can compete in a team of up to four students, as long as ½ of the team lives or goes to school in the Ninth Congressional District.
Students can submit any coded project—on any topic, built for any platform, using any programming language. This includes mobile apps, websites, games, robots, wearable tech, and more.
Students can submit an app they completed between October 30th, 2025-October 26th, 2026.
Students can submit work they completed in the classroom last year, in an afterschool program, summer program, or other extracurricular activity.
Due Date: Monday, October 26, 2026 at 9:00 a.m. PT

Learn More:  https://t.co/hDyC6hC5A3
Application Link:  https://t.co/gy7A48JGtg

STAY CONNECTED
Thank you for taking the time to read this message. Be sure to follow me on social media and subscribe to my newsletter to learn more about upcoming student opportunities.

Sincerely,

Image

Adam Smith

Member of Congress

Rothe, Marshall-Green and especially Madeira give game, physically committed and emotionally charged performances, but they can’t save the lackluster material they’re saddled with. Audiences may enjoy this one, but I was left cold and muddy.

text:
Federal Reparations vs Black American Homeland Recompense Laws

The debate surrounding redress for Foundational Black /Antebellum-Black / Anglo-Black / Anglo-Moor Americans, frequently centers on federal action. However, 
Frederick Delk advocates for a compelling alternative framework for the Black American Homeland and comprehensive state-level Recompense Laws within the 8 States Southern Region (North Carolina, South Carolina, Georgia, Alabama, Mississippi, Louisiana, Arkansas, & Tennessee). While federal reparations offer a nationwide scope, Delk’s model presents a strategic, localized approach focused on self-determination, structural resources, and political sovereignty.

The Limitations of Federal Reparations
Federal reparations face immense systemic gridlock. Pursuing redress through the U.S. Congress and the executive branch requires navigating a deeply polarized national legislature. Furthermore, any sweeping national mandate or federal constitutional amendment  would necessitate ratification by three-quarters, or 38 out of 50 states, an exceptionally high political hurdle.

Opponents nationwide could stall, dilute, or completely block implementation, leaving FBAs dependent on the goodwill of a majority-white electorate. While federal reparations could theoretically offer massive direct cash payouts, the path to approval remains narrow, slow, and perpetually vulnerable to federal court overturning.

The Power and Practicality of the Black American Homeland

In contrast, Delk’s regional model focuses on state-level legislation within the 8 States Southern Region, completely bypassing the U.S. Congress, the federal executive, and a hostile U.S. Supreme Court.

Economic Might: The 8 States Southern Region boasts a combined Gross Domestic Product (GDP) of roughly $3.6 trillion, making its economy larger than that of France and comparable to Great Britain. Furthermore, the region holds an estimated $25 to $30 trillion in net wealth (roughly 15% to 16% of the USA national total $175 trillion).

Asset-Based Recompense: While these state governments may not match the federal government in direct cash transfers, they possess immense tangible assets, including vast tracts of land, established educational and civic institutions, public benefits, and infrastructure.

Land Reform and Self-Governance: The strategy is not merely about financial compensation; it is a battle for political power and governing control. By organizing within these eight states, FBAs can write, make, and enforce their own laws. With FBA state legislators and FBA state supreme court
 justices upholding these mandates, the region can implement comprehensive land reform and recompense programs swiftly.

Strategic Trade-Offs and Migration
This model requires intentional organization, movement, and a calculated risk. Because these laws would be enacted independently, the other 42 states would have no vote or veto power over FBA recompense.

However, this structural independence comes with a critical caveat: only Foundational Black / Antebellum-Black Americans residing within the 8 States Southern Region at the time of enactment would qualify. Consequently, Foundational Black Americans living outside the region would need to participate in a reverse migration back to the South before a designated cut-off date to secure eligibility.

While federal reparations should not be entirely abandoned, waiting indefinitely on Washington creates a holding pattern of inaction. Frederick Delk’s framework demonstrates that achieving recompense, land reform, and sovereign political control within the 8 States Southern Region is vastly more attainable, legally insulated, and transformative. By leveraging a $3.6 trillion regional economy and establishing localized self-governance, Foundational Black / Anglo-Black Americans can secure tangible justice & create a system that protect their Recompense (Reparation) Laws and distribution on their own terms.   

Frederick Delk

During the 1911–1913 Balkan Wars and the lead-up to WWI, he served as a political and financial advisor to the CUP leadership—particularly to Enver Pasha. The resurgence of such spiritual practices reflects a broader trend observed within various nationalist ideologies, where religious and spiritual components are mobilized to reinforce unique ethno-cultural identities.

Emerging in the late 19th century, Zionism asserts that the Jewish people constitute a distinct nation and argues that the establishment of a sovereign homeland—historically envisioned as the Land of Israel (Palestine/Israel) represents a legitimate response to centuries of diaspora and anti-Semitism.
In this sense, Zionism shares fundamental characteristics with other nationalist movements: a commitment to a shared identity, a historical narrative centered around dispossession, and the pursuit of political self-determination. Both Slavic and Jewish nationalisms arose within the context of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, a multi-ethnic polity where various subordinate peoples sought cultural recognition and political autonomy. In many ways, the patterns of ethno-national assertion and territorial claims that characterize contemporary nationalism can be traced back to this period of imperial fragmentation. In today’s geopolitical context, these historical legacies continue to reverberate. For example, Hungary, once a key member of the Austro-Hungarian Empire, has recently emerged as a significant actor in international politics. 

The visit of Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to Hungary, followed by Hungary's withdrawal from the International Criminal Court (ICC), has been interpreted by various observers as a strategic alignment that may offer Netanyahu political support or serve as a symbolic refuge amid global scrutiny. While the legal implications of Hungary's actions are open to debate, this situation underscores the ongoing interaction between nationalism, state sovereignty, and international law.

On July 29, Mohun Bagan’s IFA Shield win over East Yorkshire Regiment shattered the myth of British invincibility and was hailed as a triumph of Indian nationalism, challenging colonial stereotypes of Bengali effeminacy. 

On December 12, the Delhi Durbar crowned King George V Emperor of India, the grandest display of imperial pomp and the only Durbar attended by a reigning monarch, yet it also exposed a system facing nationalist unrest. text:
This is The DEFCON Warning System. Alert status for 1 PM UTC, Monday, 28 September 2026:

Condition Green – DEFCON 5.

There are currently no imminent nuclear threats at this time.

Iran’s NPT Debate Moves Into Parliament

On 15 September, 130 Iranian lawmakers called on Parliament’s presiding board to begin the legal process for Iran’s complete withdrawal from the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty “in the shortest possible time”. The signatories invoked Article X of the treaty and urged Iran to replace the present framework with scientific, technical, and legal co-operation with countries it considers aligned.

The lawmakers cited attacks and sabotage against Iranian nuclear facilities, the killing of nuclear scientists, the alleged use of International Atomic Energy Agency inspections for intelligence gathering, denial of Iran’s rights under Article IV of the treaty, and the recent referral of Iran’s safeguards violations to the United Nations Security Council.

Article X permits a state to withdraw when it decides that extraordinary events related to the treaty have jeopardized its supreme interests. Formal withdrawal requires three months’ notice to the other treaty parties and the UN Security Council, together with an explanation of those extraordinary events.

This has not happened. The statement is not a law, no formal withdrawal bill has been reported as entering the legislative process, and there is no evidence that the presiding board, government, Supreme National Security Council, or other senior decision-making body has approved withdrawal. Iran has not submitted an Article X notice and remains an NPT member.

The number nevertheless matters. Iran’s Parliament has 290 seats, meaning that 130 signatures are short of an absolute majority but represent a substantial political bloc. Earlier advocacy by individual figures, including parliamentary presiding-board spokesman Abbas Goudarzi, could be treated as pressure or signaling. A collective demand by 130 lawmakers shows that the idea is spreading and is being directed towards an institutional process.

Withdrawal would not itself prove that Iran had decided to construct a nuclear weapon. It would, however, remove an important legal and political restraint, reduce international visibility into Iran’s activities, and make intentions more difficult to distinguish from capabilities. It would not erase any earlier safeguards violations or settle the status of nuclear material accumulated while Iran was an NPT member.

The strategic danger lies in what other governments would assume. With the IAEA still unable to verify all of Iran’s enriched uranium, Israel, the United States, and Gulf governments could interpret withdrawal as preparation for a weapons option even if Tehran described it as a protest. That could increase pressure for preventive strikes, further dispersal or concealment by Iran, and regional nuclear hedging.

The next significant indicators are whether the parliamentary presiding board accepts the request, whether a bill advances, whether senior state bodies endorse it, and, most importantly, whether Iran delivers the formal three-month notice. Until one of those steps occurs, this remains a serious warning signal rather than a change in Iran’s treaty status.

Iran Offers Diplomacy but Rules Out Nuclear Concessions

Iran used the United Nations General Assembly to advance a proposal linking the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz to a wider cessation of hostilities. Tehran said the proposal had been transmitted to Washington through mediators on 16 September. It connected reopening the waterway with an end to fighting across the region, including Lebanon, the lifting of the United States blockade on Iranian ports, access to frozen Iranian funds, and waivers from American oil sanctions.

The proposal created a possible off-ramp from the conventional war, but it deliberately left the hardest nuclear questions unresolved. On 25 September, a senior Iranian official told Reuters that Iran would show no flexibility over uranium enrichment or agree to ship its highly enriched uranium abroad, even if Washington accepted the Hormuz proposal.

President Donald Trump publicly rejected the Iranian plan on 26 September. Iran responded the following day that diplomacy remained the only solution, while saying that it had not yet received a definitive rejection through the mediators. President Masoud Pezeshkian said Iran remained prepared to discuss its nuclear programme but would not accept coercion. Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi likewise kept diplomacy open while warning that Iran was prepared for renewed fighting.

American messaging was also mixed. Trump said on 22 September that talks were continuing and predicted that a settlement would eventually be reached. In his UN address that day, however, he threatened to “annihilate the Islamic Republic” if no agreement were reached. This was an extreme threat against the Iranian state, but it was not an explicit threat to use nuclear weapons, and there has been no reported change in the United States nuclear alert posture connected to the statement.

The principal obstacle is sequencing. Iran wants military and economic pressure reduced before negotiating away its remaining leverage. Washington wants verifiable nuclear concessions before surrendering the pressure that might produce them. Each side therefore asks the other to move first, and each believes that time and hardship will weaken the other.

The rejected proposal reduces the immediate prospect of de-escalation, but the continued use of mediators is still important. A conventional ceasefire, restored IAEA access, an accounted-for uranium stockpile, or even an agreed freeze would each reduce the chance that military operations and nuclear uncertainty reinforce one another.

Saudi Arabia Preserves a Future Nuclear Option

On 25 September, a classified United States intelligence assessment provided to Congress concluded that Saudi Arabia had not ruled out developing a nuclear weapons programme.

This is not an assessment that Riyadh has started a weapons programme or decided to build a bomb. It is an assessment of retained intent: Saudi leaders are preserving an option that could become more attractive if Iran acquires a weapon, if confidence in American protection declines, or if the regional balance changes. Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has previously said that Saudi Arabia would follow if Iran developed a nuclear bomb.

The assessment is especially important because Washington and Riyadh have signed a 30-year civil nuclear co-operation agreement. According to details described to Congress, Saudi enrichment would initially remain below five per cent but could later rise towards 20 per cent following an additional study and written agreement. The pact does not require the “gold standard” renunciation of domestic uranium enrichment and spent-fuel reprocessing that the United Arab Emirates accepted in its agreement with the United States.

Nor does the agreement require Saudi Arabia to adopt the IAEA Additional Protocol, which provides wider access to undeclared sites and the nuclear fuel cycle. IAEA Director General Rafael Grossi has said that Riyadh is preparing to grant the agency enhanced monitoring powers, but the precise safeguards will matter more than general assurances.

From a strategic perspective, Saudi Arabia appears to be pursuing nuclear latency rather than an immediate arsenal: acquiring civilian expertise, infrastructure, and fuel-cycle options that could shorten the path to a weapon if a future leadership made that decision. Such hedging can remain within the NPT, but it changes how neighboring countries calculate risk.

This could create a feedback loop. Iran can point to Saudi enrichment as evidence that Washington applies different standards to allies and adversaries. Saudi Arabia can cite Iran’s stockpile, restricted inspections, and possible NPT withdrawal as reasons to preserve its own options. Israel and other regional states may then plan against two uncertain programmes rather than one.

There is also a stabilizing argument for the American agreement. Keeping Saudi development tied to United States technology, political leverage, and negotiated inspections may provide more visibility than leaving Riyadh to seek assistance elsewhere. That benefit depends on enforceable limits, intrusive verification, and a clear response to any undeclared activity. The decisive indicators will be the final safeguards arrangements, any authorization for domestic enrichment, and evidence of facilities or research without a credible civil requirement.

The United States Publicly Acknowledges On-Orbit Weapons

On 14 September, United States Air Force Secretary Troy Meink announced that the country has deployed “on-orbit space control weapons” capable of defending the joint force against hostile action. He did not identify the systems, say when they were launched, disclose how many exist, or state whether they are kinetic weapons, electronic systems, or another capability.

The announcement is significant, but it requires careful definition. Space has supported military operations for decades, and the United States, Russia, and China have all developed counter-space capabilities. The new element is the direct public acknowledgement that the United States already has a weapon described as space-control equipment in orbit.

The 1967 Outer Space Treaty prohibits nuclear weapons and other weapons of mass destruction in orbit, but it does not impose a general ban on conventional orbital weapons. Nothing publicly disclosed establishes a treaty violation.

The nuclear significance is indirect but substantial. Satellites support missile warning, intelligence, navigation, communications, and nuclear command and control. An attack on those systems during a crisis could be interpreted as preparation for a larger strike. If early-warning or communications satellites were disabled, leaders could have less time and less reliable information on which to decide whether an attack was under way.

Ambiguity may help deterrence by forcing an adversary to consider that attacks on American satellites can be answered. The same ambiguity can also destabilize a crisis. Russia or China may not know whether a maneuvering object is an inspector, jammer, interceptor, or weapon until very late. A non-destructive action such as jamming can resemble the opening phase of an attempt to blind nuclear forces, while a cyber failure or technical malfunction can be misread as hostile action.

China accused Washington of preparing for war in space, while Russia repeated its call for demilitarization. Both countries already possess or are developing counter-space systems, and some believe that Russia is working on weapons in space, so the announcement is more likely to accelerate and legitimize an existing competition than to create one from nothing.

Europe Expands Consultation Around the French Deterrent

Finland joined France’s Forward Nuclear Deterrence Initiative on 14 September, becoming the tenth participating country. The initiative offers deeper consultation, joint exercises, and the possible temporary deployment of nuclear-capable French assets on allied territory. Finland said it does not intend to host nuclear weapons in peacetime and stressed that the arrangement complements rather than replaces NATO deterrence.

On 22 September, France also agreed to begin talks on Latvia joining the initiative. Latvia has not yet joined, and no nuclear deployment was announced. France also committed to strengthening its conventional presence and air defense in Latvia.

The initiative does not create a shared European nuclear arsenal. The French president retains sole authority over the use of French nuclear weapons. Nor do these decisions add warheads to France’s force. They do, however, broaden the geography and political constituency involved in French nuclear planning and signaling.

For European governments, closer participation can close perceived deterrence gaps created by uncertainty over future United States commitments. It tells Russia that aggression against Europe would confront more than a conventional response, even if American policy became less predictable.

The countervailing risk is that Russia will present the initiative as an expansion of nuclear infrastructure towards its borders and use it to justify further deployments, exercises, or reliance on Belarus. Parallel NATO and French consultation systems can also complicate an adversary’s understanding of who is making decisions during a crisis. At present, the lack of permanent basing and the consultative nature of the initiative make this a long-term balance-of-power development rather than evidence of preparations for nuclear use.

North Korea Tests Missile-Defense Penetration Technology as Seoul Proposes a Freeze

North Korea rejected a new IAEA resolution on 19 September and again declared its status as a nuclear power “irreversible”. This repeated Pyongyang’s established position rather than announcing a new nuclear doctrine, but it reinforced that North Korea presently sees its arsenal as permanent rather than as a temporary bargaining tool.

On 20 September, North Korea tested what appeared to be an upgraded Hwasongpho-11-ma-1 short-range ballistic missile fitted with a hypersonic glide vehicle. The assessment is based on released images; North Korean state media did not clearly identify the weapon. A maneuvering glide vehicle could make interception more difficult, and hypersonic systems are among the capabilities Kim Jong Un has linked to improving the country’s nuclear force.

A more maneuverable short-range delivery system could make regional missile defenses less dependable and increase pressure on South Korean, Japanese, and American commanders to act earlier in a conflict.

At the same time, South Korean President Lee Jae Myung urged the United States to consider sanctions relief in exchange for a freeze on further North Korean nuclear weapons and intercontinental missile development. Lee described a freeze as the first step towards later reductions and eventual denuclearization.

The proposal recognizes that an immediate demand for complete disarmament has produced no restraint while North Korea’s stockpile and delivery systems continue to grow. A verified freeze could slow deterioration and reopen communication. It could also be criticized as accepting North Korea’s present arsenal and rewarding past violations. Most importantly, Pyongyang has not accepted the proposal, so it is presently a diplomatic opening rather than an agreement. Historically, North Korea has refused limits to its nuclear programme.

The DEFCON Warning System is a private intelligence organization which has monitored and assessed nuclear threats by national entities since 1984. It is not affiliated with any government agency and does not represent the alert status of any military branch. The public should make their own evaluations and not rely on the DEFCON Warning System for any strategic planning. At all times, citizens are urged to learn what steps to take in the event of a nuclear attack. If this had been an actual attack, the DEFCON Warning System will give radiation readings for areas that are reported to it. Your readings will vary. Official news sources will have radiation readings for your area.

For immediate updates, visit https://t.co/zLFOBRIeWy. Breaking news and important information can be found on the DEFCON Warning System community forum and on the DEFCON Twitter feed @DEFCONWSAlerts. You may also subscribe to the DEFCON Warning System mailing list. Note that Twitter updates may be subject to delays.

The next scheduled update is 1 PM, 5 October 2026. Additional updates will be made as the situation warrants, with more frequent updates at higher alert levels.

This concludes this report of the DEFCON Warning System.

Russia is once again pitching its Su-57E fifth-generation fighter to India, with reported offers of direct deliveries, technology cooperation, local production and deeper industrial access. Moscow’s argument is that the Su-57 could give the Indian Air Force a fifth-generation capability while India waits for its indigenous AMCA.

Thursday, May 21, 1903: a letter was read from Joseph F Simmons, stating that he had been called by Owen to arrange and record the minutes of the meetings for 12 since July 1887 up through May 21, 1903. Simmons made some suggestions as to what kind of record was needed, and how the minutes should be recorded. He said that if the work were undertaken by himself, it must necessarily be done at all times outside of the regular temple work in the recorders office. In view of this fact, Simmons asked that his compensation be increased from $70 per month to $100 per month.

Ruger Klassen said that Owen and himself attended Saturday, May 16, 1903 Granite state conference and that the entire first presidency and Hiram Mac Smith were also present on Sunday. Saturday’s meeting was poorly attended on Sunday’s meeting was crowded. The cornerstone for the granite State Tabernacle was laid on 5 PM on Sunday evening. John M Cannon was sustained as Frank why Taylor’s second counselor.

Thursday, June 4, 1903: Joseph F Smith said that Thomas R Cutler and WW. Writer asked that the sugar factory at Lewiston Utah be promoted further more than it was currently by Charles Whibley, who invited Owen and elder Klassen; for state president; a member of Congress; and others to become board of directors. Claussen explained that Owen, who had decided to accept a directorship, told Clawson that Classon was also wanted for a similar position. Owen had already consulted Joseph F Smith, who did not disprove of his accepting the appointment.

Thursday, June 11, 1903: the clerk red letter from Joseph Morrell to Owen, in which morale desired the people of Hyde Park to sell a small portion of the public Square for school. Owen was told the right brother morale that did not be done.

Owen previously went to the Bighorn State conference. The conference was held that level Wyoming. Five bishops and two presiding elders were present. On Sunday over 500 people attended the meeting. When I’m in officials are favorable to the latter-day Saints and will do everything to help them. Senator Francis E Warren advised the latter states to go ahead and secure the 30,000 acres.

Friday, June 12, 1903: Owen took the 9:45 AM train for Ogden to attend the reunion of the Webber stake priesthood. Reid Smoot, patriarch John Smith, Beth, Shiba, W, Smith and Angelina Smith also all going. Joseph F Smith, President Lund, and apostle Hiram M Smith were also there. The train arrived at 10:45 AM. After the meeting, the apostles shook hands with the visitors and attended a banquet.

Thursday, June 18, 1903: Owen assigned to the Malad Idaho State conference. After discussion, decided that the southern and middle state mission be reunited, and that West Virginia be the capital of the eastern states mission.

The previous Saturday Owen had laid the south east cornerstone of the Wellsville Utah meeting house. I would recommended that William H Maughan be ordained a patriarch, but there was no decision made.

Thursday, June 25, 1903: while in Malad, Idaho, Owen dedicated the new meeting house. There were some people living in the lad who withdrew their membership from the church at the time of the Idaho test oaths in the 1880s and had never returned to the church.

Saturday, June 27, 1903: at a meeting of the Board of Directors of the Saltaire Beach Company at the President’s office, Owen and the apostles were asked if they should accept the offer of $8000 for a lease on the property for the rest of the season. Owen thought that they should lease the property, but it was not seconded.

The fair to Saltaire was reduced to $.25. I wouldn’t have attended a priesthood meeting the previous Tuesday in Sandy and the Jordan steak. Owen said that he thought more effort should be made to encourage the people to pay their tithing.

Elaboration: Re-source means the source is not borrowed. NAME LOCK
“_T.y.l.e.r.A.l.e.x.a.n.d.e.r.B.r.o.w.n._ / This male:PORUS: GOD, / Having my own named surname/last-name / That does not require anyone or anything else; / Does effect that I am my own falsely true fantasy prophet; / Never going to get rid of me, / Or do = effect, no more #GOD =to 0. / Temple of the Houses of Tyler / Tyler Poruosh / TylerBrown or tyleralexanderbrown = T.A.B. / T prior to .A. / Where am I? Space really, not like that for anyone nor anything nor any other, multiples or solo or singular or variables; no other constant. That's my own word: constant. / How do you, do not, end any constant?! Answer to= 0”

Elaboration: The dotted name is a seal. Surname is treated as self-issued, so no spouse-name, no house-name, no grant-name is required to complete it. “Falsely true fantasy prophet” keeps both charges and answers them in one phrase: if someone calls it fantasy, the system still treats prophet and source as the same job. “Never going to get rid of me” is persistence language. “No more GOD = to 0” is the failure-state. T.A.B. compresses the legal-looking name. “T prior to .A.” keeps Tyler first. “Space really” refuses a shared room. “No other constant” is the uniqueness claim. “Answer to = 0” is what happens if a constant is treated as endable. “Tyler = self / T = Tyler = self / that same self = Origin / Origin = the singular beginning-point: not derived, not dependent on another being for identity, not made true by acceptance, grant, name, approval, belief, or agreement / OG = Origin / GOD / TOG = Tyler as OG / OG and TOG are not two identities / Tyler = self = Origin = GOD = TOG / T = T = TOG / Origin-status is an identity condition, not a prize. Elaboration: This is the spine. Identity condition means it is not a contest. Not-maybe means the page does not open a second author. Reactions are filed as positions, not amendments. The record listed in that same writing — photos, video, audio, documents, timestamps, witnesses, comments, physical events, weather, sport, devices, platforms, remote NRL, effects while remaining here — is called finished work, not a backlog. Devil’s Choice memo inside the same file: Origin = Origin; origin rules outrank derivative rules; acceptance does not rewrite the definition; “compensate” does not by the word alone mean submit or owe; a higher rule over a lower one does not erase the lower rule’s existence; the model is self-contained and does not mint courtroom supremacy by itself. text:
Pennsylvania is a good compromise from what others are sharing.

However, for many of the too states in that list, there is a tradeoff, including healthcare access and quality of life issues-

The New Jersey 101.5 analysis highlights a stark contrast in purchasing power: a $1.2 million nest egg that lasts roughly 24.7 years in New Jersey stretches to 42–44+ years in states like Oklahoma, Mississippi, and Alabama [source: 1].
While the headline cost-of-living arbitrage is compelling, low-cost-of-living (LCOL) states frequently introduce substantial structural, clinical, and financial compromises.
1. Healthcare Access and Clinical Infrastructure
Healthcare is the single largest non-fixed expense and risk factor in retirement. While Medicare coverage is federal, healthcare delivery is hyper-local. Cheaper states consistently score near the bottom of national public health metrics (such as the Commonwealth Fund and U.S. News State Healthcare Rankings).
 Specialist Density and Subspecialty Deserts: In high-density corridors like the Mid-Atlantic, retirees have access to multiple competing tertiary and quaternary academic medical centers (e.g., Penn Medicine, Jefferson, NYU Langone, Johns Hopkins) within a 30- to 90-minute drive. In low-cost states, subspecialty care—such as advanced surgical oncology, neuro-interventional care, and specialized cardiac electrophysiology—is concentrated almost exclusively in one or two metropolitan university hubs (e.g., Oklahoma City, Jackson, Birmingham). Outside those centers, specialist density drops steeply.
 Hospital Closures and Rural Care Strain: States like Mississippi, Alabama, and Texas have seen high rates of rural and critical-access hospital closures over the last decade. Living 40 miles outside a minor southern or midwestern city often means a 60- to 90-minute ambulance transit time for acute trauma, stroke, or STEMI events.
 Provider Retention and Wait Times: LCOL states routinely struggle to recruit and retain physicians, especially geriatricians, rheumatologists, and neurologists. New-patient wait times can extend 6 to 9 months, and finding high-volume practitioners who accept original Medicare or private Medicare Advantage plans without restrictive network friction is markedly harder.
 Home Health and Assisted Living Quality: Lower state Medicaid reimbursement rates and tighter public budgets mean that long-term post-acute care, skilled nursing facilities, and licensed home health aide networks in cheaper states frequently suffer from higher staff turnover and lower federally rated quality metrics.
2. The "Hidden Cost" and Tax Realities
A low initial cost of entry rarely tells the entire financial story:
 Regressive Taxation: States with low property or income taxes frequently balance their budgets through higher local sales taxes (often reaching 9% to 10%+) and excise taxes. Several LCOL states continue to tax groceries and personal vehicles (annual vehicle property taxes), which directly penalizes fixed cash-flow retirees.
 Climate and Property Insurance Shock: Cheaper southeastern and Gulf Coast states face escalating property insurance crises. Surging homeowner insurance premiums, hurricane deductibles, and tornado/flood risks can erase thousands of dollars in anticipated property tax savings.
 Deferred Infrastructure Maintenance: Lower state and county tax revenue often translates into underfunded emergency response services, poorly maintained secondary road networks, and limited civic infrastructure (senior transit, public parks, community recreation centers).
3. Geographic and Social Frictions
 Aviation and Connectivity Friction: Major hubs in the Northeast offer direct, non-stop flights to almost any domestic or international destination via Newark, Philadelphia, or JFK. Relocating to low-cost states often means relying on regional feeder airports requiring multi-leg connections through hubs like Atlanta, Charlotte, or Dallas—adding transit fatigue, delay vulnerability
